reason: B is the stronger proposal because it identifies the physically relevant segregation driver—surface free-energy differences—and provides testable size/heating-rate comparisons with correlated composition and melting measurements. Its cited evidence is only indirect and the proposed ~20 nm boundary is unsupported, but A incorrectly attributes segregation to Cu’s low melting point, assumes annealing will homogenize rather than potentially enhance segregation, and supplies no requested prior-nanoparticle evidence.
